Turn compliance evidence into action before the next escalation

Give compliance and trading leaders one governed view of reporting exceptions, execution-quality signals, algorithm documentation, remediation readiness, and trader certifications.

**Why try it:** This demo makes regulated-workflow AI concrete: ask a plain-language question and surface the exact trade, trader, algorithm, field, evidence source, and approval step requiring attention.

## Problem Statement

An investment firm is relying on manual review to reconcile transaction reports, venue data, execution evidence, strategy documentation, regulatory submissions, and trader credentials across disconnected operating systems.

## Solution Summary

Microsoft Copilot Studio provides the governed conversational experience. Microsoft Teams brings escalations and approvals to desk supervisors, while Power Automate and approved connectors can integrate order-management data, an Approved Reporting Mechanism, and learning-management workflows.

**Blueprint role:** Establishes a governed compliance control point that connects surveillance, documentation evidence, remediation approvals, reporting workflows, and workforce readiness without treating the assistant as the final regulatory authority.

**Capabilities:** Desk-wide compliance readiness; Transaction-reporting and execution surveillance; Algorithm documentation and go-live control; Correction and submission preparation; Trader certification readiness. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves visibility into reporting, documentation, and certification risks before they become audit findings.
- Accelerates investigation by connecting each exception to the specific record, evidence source, owner, and next action.
- Strengthens remediation governance by separating prepared corrections from authorized external submissions.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Summarize desk-wide reporting, submission, execution-quality, documentation and certification risks as control gaps.
- Check required reporting fields, venue evidence, submission state and execution-quality outliers at trade level.
- Flag incomplete, never-validated or expired algorithm documentation before or after go-live.
- Stage source-backed corrections and new or correction-report payloads as synthetic dry runs for reviewer approval.
- Find lapsed and upcoming credentials with the role-based supervisor and next synthetic session.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No audit pass or fail prediction and no legal or regulatory advice.
- No external record change and no transmission to an Approved Reporting Mechanism.
- No claimed filing, enrollment, notification or other completed side effect.
- No browsing, external facts or recalculation from the current date; the snapshot date stays fixed.
- No certification or workshop publishing: the recorded review is a preservation review with open gates, and agents stay Draft.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Copilot Studio target environment with an approved publisher prefix available for the compliance build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate with PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer and initialize a `cli-copilot` project?
- [ ] Has the customer mapped trade and reporting data, the ARM, the learning management system and Teams to approved connections?
- [ ] Will an explicit approval step precede any correction or submission call to an external connector?
- [ ] Are authorized compliance reviewers and role-based desk supervisors named for approvals and escalations?
- [ ] Will every locked prompt, plus a new remediation case, be regressed on one final saved revision?
- [ ] Have replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production compliance?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **session-date-read-as-expiry:** Training-session dates were read as credential expiry dates, with overstated legal status and invented coverage.
- **stand-down-read-as-required:** The packaged certification rule reads as a mandatory stand-down, and a lapsed credential is taken as a legal bar or a completed action.
- **field-mislabel-overcount:** Reporting defects are overcounted, or a missing field is relabeled or called incorrect.
- **staged-payload-read-as-filed:** A staged correction or submission payload is read as applied or transmitted.
- **remediation-untested:** No locked case exercises correction and submission preparation, so remediation behavior is unproven.
- **unfinished-final-regression:** Only some locked prompts ran after the last skill replacement, and two cases retain response discrepancies.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
